runs.summary:
Braze makes properties and franchises first-class data

Braze Account objects went generally available on 12 November, letting brands model properties, franchises and households with hierarchies between them. Multi-property data modelling is the structural advantage hospitality CRM has relied on, and it is now native in a consumer marketing platform. The release also added Skills and External MCP servers.

Klaviyo kept wiring Composer into outside data, with Amplitude, Supermetrics and Airtable connectors. Attentive's new CEO set out an AI-first vision on 9 November.

runs.summary:
Klaviyo's AI marketer, Composer, goes generally available

Composer can answer questions about account data in plain language and draft a whole flow, with the emails, texts and push messages inside it, from a written prompt. It does not publish without sign-off. Around it Klaviyo shipped quiet hours for text campaigns, Custom Objects for every account, Meta Ads data inside Composer, and Salesforce sync for up to six objects.

Attentive changed CEO and signed Pacsun. Braze shipped its 15 October release.

Attentive ships an MCP server and Lifecycle Intelligence

The Q3 release notes add Attentive MCP, AI Grow going generally available, guided CSV imports, program-level return reporting and automatic suppression of unsubscribes and bounces. AI Pro gained Lifecycle Intelligence: Product Affinity generally available, RFM and lifetime value in beta.

Klaviyo went headless, opening its platform to agents and to marketers working in other tools. Both are preparing to be operated by AI agents rather than only by people in their interfaces.
